meta.title: King Solomon's Mine: The Paris Codex
meta.notes: 30 sections (S01–S30) with consistently deep prose. Good/Bad/Special endings. All endings return to S01.
meta.blurb: A book with a hidden map draws you to a secret Paris library, then down into catacombs and caverns where King Solomon's treasure waits with teeth.

S01.text:
You find the book the way trouble always finds you: quietly, and then all at once.

It sits on the bottom shelf of a cramped estate sale, wedged between hymnals and a water-stained atlas. The cover is cracked leather, the title rubbed nearly smooth, and the pages smell like dust that has had a century to settle.

When you open it, you expect sermons or genealogy. Instead, you find margin notes in tight handwriting, ink that looks too deliberate to be idle. The last page holds a pasted pocket, and inside the pocket is something that should not be there.

A folded map, thin as onion skin, inked in red and black. Along the edge, a line of Latin you can barely translate without moving your lips: not a warning exactly, more like an invitation you are supposed to regret accepting.

And at the center of the map, a symbol that pulls at your attention like a magnet: a six-pointed seal ringed with tiny marks, and beneath it two words in English, blunt and modern.

KING SOLOMON.

S02.text:
You spread the map across your kitchen table and weigh it down with whatever is heavy and honest: a mug, a paperweight, your own hands.

The ink is not decorative. It is instruction. There are rail lines sketched in faint gray, street names in French, and a single building marked with an X that looks like it was stabbed into the paper rather than drawn.

Paris. A specific arrondissement. A library that does not appear on tourist lists. The map doesn't say 'go here.' It assumes you will.

In the margins, a list of symbols repeats, each paired with a number: a key, a torch, a crown, a door, a serpent. You have seen puzzle-notation like this before in field journals and wartime ciphers. It's the language of people who expect to be interrupted.

You notice a crease pattern that doesn't match the folds. When you tilt the paper under light, the fibers reveal a second layer of ink, faint and ghostlike: a corridor drawn beneath the library outline, spiraling down.

Your pulse speeds up. This isn't a treasure map. It's a descent.

S03.text:
You call the only person you trust to tell you the truth without trying to own it: a contact who lives half in universities and half in back rooms.

They answer on the second ring, voice clipped. You can hear papers moving, a keyboard, the faint hum of a life spent digging through archives.

You describe the book. The map. The seal. The words King Solomon. There's a pause that lasts just long enough to be bad news.

'That seal shows up in a handful of private collections,' your contact says. 'Mostly rumors. Mostly stolen. It's tied to a set of travel notes from the early 1900s. A French bibliophile named Laurent Vauclair. He vanished. So did his research.'

You ask what Vauclair was chasing. Your contact exhales. 'A legend inside a legend. That Solomon's treasure wasn't just gold. That it was a system. A vault with rules.'

And then the part that tightens your throat: 'If you have a real map, you're not the first one to touch it. Someone will come looking.'

Your kitchen feels smaller. The book feels heavier.

S04.text:
Paris hits you like it always does: beauty on top, machinery underneath.

The city smells of coffee, exhaust, rain on stone. You cross bridges built by kings and walk past tourists who think history is only what sits above ground.

The map leads you to a narrow street where the buildings lean inward like conspirators. A small brass plate marks the place: a private reading society, invitation only. The kind of 'library' that collects forbidden books the way other people collect art.

You step inside and the air changes. It is quieter, thicker, saturated with paper and polish. The front desk clerk looks you over the way a customs officer does: not judging, assessing.

You show the book. Not the map. The clerk's eyes flick to the cracked leather like they've seen it before. They say nothing, only lift a finger and point down a side corridor lined with portraits that stare too hard.

You walk past those eyes and feel the city above you vanish. Whatever is under this place is what the map wants you to find.

And you are now committed in the way that matters: not by a signature, but by proximity.

choices.label: ASK FOR ACCESS TO RESTRICTED STACKS

S05.text:
You play the respectable angle. You approach the clerk with calm hands and a calm voice, the way you approach a guard dog you intend to pet and pass.

'I'm looking for Laurent Vauclair,' you say, letting the name land like a test.

The clerk's face doesn't change, but something in the room tightens. A subtle shift: a book closing somewhere, a footstep pausing, a breath held.

'We don't keep membership records for strangers,' the clerk replies. Their politeness is not kindness. It is a wall.

You slide the book across the counter and open it to the back pocket, letting a corner of the map show. Not enough to be stolen in a blink. Enough to be recognized.

For the first time, the clerk's eyes show interest. Not greed. Recognition. A careful professional interest, like a locksmith seeing a rare key.

'Follow me,' they say softly.

They lead you through a door that should not be there, into a stairwell that descends in a spiral, the walls lined with plaques naming donors who never existed. The library has layers. You are being allowed into one.

choices.label: BACK OUT AND TRY ANOTHER WAY

S06.text:
You choose motion over permission. In places like this, permission is often a leash.

You drift toward the back rooms with the practiced casualness of someone looking for a restroom. The corridor narrows. The carpet becomes older. The lights dim.

A locked door blocks you. The keyhole is antique, the kind that expects a thin piece of metal and patience. You produce a pick set you promised yourself you'd never need again.

The lock yields with a soft, satisfying click. Inside is a cramped storage room stacked with archival boxes and rolled rugs. It smells like mothballs and secrets.

At the far end, behind a hanging tapestry, you find another door—iron, modern, out of place. A keypad beside it glows faintly.

A keypad in a library is a confession: something valuable is hidden below.

You press your ear to the door. You hear nothing. That's the worst kind of silence. It means the place is designed to swallow sound.

choices.label: SEARCH THE ROOM FOR A CODE

S07.text:
The door opens the way a mouth opens: reluctant, then wide.

Stone steps descend into cold air. The walls are older than the building above, older than the street. Your flashlight beam catches damp limestone and faint chalk marks that could be centuries old or yesterday's.

The secret chamber at the bottom is small and precise, like a workshop for quiet crimes. A reading table stands in the center, its surface scarred by blades and ink. Shelves hold ledgers bound in black cloth, titles written in codes instead of letters.

In the far corner, a metal grate covers a shaft. Warm air rises from below, smelling of earth and mineral, deeper and different than the library's paper-smell.

There is a plaque on the wall with a simple phrase in French: 'Knowledge has weight.' Someone scratched a second phrase beneath it with a knife: 'So does greed.'

Your map's symbols start to make sense. Key. Torch. Door. Serpent. Crown. This is not a single puzzle. It's a sequence.

And you feel it—the first real warning in your bones. You're not alone in the hunt. You are just early.

S08.text:
You open the ledgers with the reverence of a thief handling a relic.

The handwriting inside matches the book's margin notes. Laurent Vauclair. Dates. Coordinates. Sketches of tunnels that spiral beneath Paris like veins beneath skin.

The entries are not romantic. They are terrified. 'The library is a mask,' one line reads. 'Beneath it, the city becomes an organ. It digests.'

You find references to a 'second library' in the depths, a place where symbols were carved into stone and the air felt wrong, as if the earth itself remembered something it wished to forget.

In the final pages, Vauclair writes about 'Solomon's Mines' not as a location but as a concept: a hidden corridor of wealth and traps built by a man who understood that thieves are inevitable. The vault isn't meant to be sealed. It's meant to test.

Loose in the ledger is a paper strip with numbers arranged like a poem. It looks like a keypad code. You slip it into your pocket.

Outside the chamber, you hear a faint sound. A footstep above. Someone else is in the library now, and they are moving with purpose.

choices.label: HIDE AND WAIT FOR THEM TO PASS

S09.text:
You lift the grate and the shaft breathes up at you, warm and damp.

A ladder descends into darkness. The metal rungs are slick, and each one feels like a decision being made again. Paris recedes above you, replaced by the slow, ancient pressure of stone.

Halfway down, your light catches graffiti—names, dates, crude drawings—proof that people have always wanted to mark the underworld. Then the graffiti stops, and the walls become clean again. That boundary is deliberate.

You step off into a tunnel that smells of wet chalk and old bone. The catacombs have a particular flavor of dread: an orderly death, stacked and labeled, a city storing its past where it can't be seen.

This tunnel isn't the tourist route. It is narrower, rougher, purposeful. Your beam glints off small metal plates set into the floor like scales.

The map's serpent symbol repeats in your mind. Scales. Sequence. A lock disguised as a threat.

S10.text:
You kill your light and become part of the stone.

A door opens above. Someone steps down into the stairwell. The footfalls are measured, not rushed—professional. A flashlight beam sweeps the chamber, pausing on the ledgers, then the grate.

A low voice murmurs, amused: 'Vauclair wasn't wrong. The map always finds another hand.'

The beam moves away. Steps retreat. Only then do you breathe again, lungs aching from restraint.

When you relight your flashlight, the room feels smaller. Your hunt now has a shadow, and shadows make every choice sharper.

S11.text:
You step around the plates, keeping your weight on rough stone. Your heel brushes one by accident. A tiny click answers.

Dust sifts down. Somewhere ahead, a chain rattles once. Still no explosion, no dart, no obvious punishment. That is the worst kind of mercy.

Then you notice thin slits in the wall at knee and shoulder height. Inside one slit, something metallic glints—points waiting.

The plates aren't a trap in themselves. They're a pattern. Step wrong, and the slits speak.

You pull out the map and match the serpent symbol to its number. A sequence. You can do sequences. You can do rules.

You kneel, steady your breath, and commit to solving what a paranoid king built to punish thieves with manners.

S12.text:
You decide not to gamble with a floor designed by someone who thought cruelty was craft.

You backtrack and search the walls for seams. In underground places, there are always seams—patches, repairs, admissions.

Your light catches a cleaner line of mortar. You press your fingers to it and feel air: a draft. Promise.

You pry the mortar away and reveal a crawl space barely wide enough for shoulders. Tight spaces turn bravery into panic, but they also dodge the proud traps.

You slide in, stone scraping your jacket. The air warms as you descend. The rock changes color. Timber supports appear like ribs.

When the crawl space opens, you are no longer in the catacombs. You are in an older cut—dark rock, reinforced, mined.

You have crossed from Paris's underworld into something that was built to keep history in a box.

S13.text:
You study the plates like a chessboard. Each bears a tiny mark: torch, key, door, serpent, crown.

It reads like a story: light, access, passage, danger, reward. You step onto torch. Nothing. Key. Click. Door. Another click.

When you step onto serpent, the floor's tension shifts as if satisfied. Crown locks last. The wall slits grind closed, quietly, like a judge putting away a knife.

Ahead, the tunnel slopes down into a cavern where old rail tracks gleam faintly. Heat shimmers in the air.

Behind you, you swear you hear another footfall echoing your sequence. Someone is following, and they learned from you.

You move anyway. The mine doesn't care who is clever. It cares who survives.

S14.text:
The corridor opens into a cavern so large your light can't find its edges.

Old rails cut through silt. Timber supports rise like ribs. Tool marks in the walls speak of hand chisels and stubborn patience.

You dig a coin from rubble—thick, heavy, stamped with a seal you now recognize. Not a souvenir. A marker of ownership.

The air tastes metallic, mineral-rich, like blood after you bite your tongue. A faint smoke smell rides it, impossible unless something still burns deeper down.

In the cavern's center is a descending shaft ringed with steps. Above it, the seal repeats. Your map points down with the confidence of a trap that expects you to obey.

Treasure below. Danger below. The mine doesn't care which you came for.

S15.text:
You follow the rails because rails mean someone once expected to carry heavy things out of here.

The tunnel curves. Warmth pulses in waves like a furnace breathing. You pass rusted carts and shattered lanterns half-buried in dust.

You see footprints. Fresh. Not yours. The sight tightens your stomach more than any trap ever could.

A side alcove holds a broken camp: torn pack, smashed canteen, a blood smear across stone. No body. The mine took what it wanted and left the rest unresolved.

Deeper in, you hear a scrape—metal on stone—then silence. Either a person hiding, or a mechanism waking.

Your light feels suddenly loud. You lower it and listen with your skin.

S16.text:
You set a choke point with loose stones, a crude barrier meant to slow someone rushing through.

You wait in shadow, blade in hand. Patience is an ugly kind of courage, but it works.

A figure approaches in a climbing harness, face half-covered. Their flashlight sweeps the tunnel like they're reading it.

They sigh at your stones, step aside, and slip through a second passage you didn't notice, moving around your trap like water around a rock.

Before you can react, they strike your wrist, clean and practiced. Your blade drops. A weapon presses to your ribs.

Their whisper is almost friendly: 'You're late. And you're in my mine.'

S17.text:
You descend the central shaft, stone slick beneath your boots. The temperature rises in waves, like lungs breathing you in.

Inscriptions line the inner wall: names and symbols. Torch. Key. Crown. A roster of attempts, recorded with blunt honesty.

At the bottom, the chamber glows dim orange from mineral veins in the rock, ember-light without flame.

A metal door stands there, ancient and patterned, sealed with the same six-pointed mark. No handle. Only rotating rings etched with the symbols from your map.

This is a vault built by someone who expected thieves. And expected them to believe they deserved what was inside.

You place your hands on the rings and feel how cold they are, like a promise that doesn't care about your warmth.

S18.text:
You drift into a natural cavern where water drips into a pool that reflects your light like an eye.

A narrow stone bridge crosses the pool. Along its sides are evenly spaced holes—vents or dart ports. The bridge is too neat to trust.

On the far side, amber glow leaks from a corridor. The vault chamber is close enough to warm your face.

Then a whisper rises behind you: 'Don't step on the third stone. It drops you into the pool.'

Your pulse spikes. Someone is here with you—helping, hunting, or both. In a place like this, motives change as fast as grip.

You swallow, and decide whether to trust the warning or trust only yourself.

choices.label: TRUST THE WARNING AND CROSS CAREFULLY

S19.text:
You meet the other explorer in torchlight and realize they're real, steady, and dangerous in the quiet way.

They call themselves Sable, like it's a mask they've worn long enough to forget the face underneath.

They tell you Vauclair mapped the descent, not the exit. They want proof, and an artifact small enough to pocket.

They offer a deal with gambler ease: open it together, split what makes sense, and don't stab each other until daylight.

A deal in the dark is always a blade with velvet on it, but it might be the only way you open the vault without dying alone.

You nod once, and feel the mine watch your agreement like it cares about contracts.

S20.text:
The vault door's rings are cold under your fingers despite the heat in the chamber.

You align torch with key. Click. Door with serpent. Deeper click. The mineral veins brighten as if the mine is paying attention.

The last alignment is crown. You hesitate, because crowns change people. Then you turn the ring.

The door exhales ancient air and begins to open with a groan like something waking from a long sleep.

Warm shimmer spills from within, reflecting off surfaces you can't fully see yet. Your mouth goes dry, not from fear, but from wanting.

You step forward and feel the mine's patience tighten, as if it expects you to hurry and be punished for it.

S21.text:
The vault is a cathedral built for greed.

Shelves carved into stone hold chalices, sealed jars, scroll cases, coins stacked into careful towers. Gold is everywhere, but it isn't the first thing you notice.

The first thing you notice is the smell: cedar, resin, old metal, and something faintly sweet like incense burned for show.

At the center is a dais and a smaller chest banded in metal. The seal repeats on it like a command.

A thin boundary line circles the dais. Cross it and you accept terms. The vault is offering you a fair chance to ruin yourself.

You step closer and feel the orange glow pulse in slow rhythm, like a heartbeat deciding whether you deserve to keep yours.

S22.text:
You pause at the threshold and force yourself to do the boring thing: look.

The floor is too clean. Hair-thin grooves lead from the boundary line toward the walls, channels designed to carry something worse than water.

Near the doorframe you find a counterweight mechanism hidden behind carved stone. Cross too fast and the door begins to close. Cross with care and it stays open.

You step over the line slowly. The vault does not move. The grooves stay quiet. The room accepts restraint like a lion accepts a handler who doesn't smell like panic.

If Sable is with you, they give a quiet nod. If you're alone, the silence is heavier, but your decision is the same: survive first, marvel second.

The sealed chest waits on the dais like a question that only has expensive answers.

S23.text:
The seal on the chest is not wax. It's metal, fused into the banding, etched with the mark and tiny letters around it.

There is a keyhole shaped like a ring. You remember the brass ring fused into stone in the shaft. You remember Vauclair's note about weight.

If Sable is with you, they produce a ring from a pocket and roll it across their knuckles. 'Found it on a corpse,' they say, with a smile that doesn't ask forgiveness.

You insert the ring. It fits like fate. You twist. The seal releases with a soft snap, almost relieved.

Inside is not a mountain of gold. It's a single signet ring set with a stone that looks like cooled fire, engraved with the seal.

The ring radiates authority, like a key that doesn't just open doors but makes doors want to open.

You understand: this is the real treasure. Not wealth. Power over passage. A key to vaults. And keys create more problems than gold ever does.

S24.text:
You scan the shelves like a scholar pretending not to be a thief.

Artifacts don't belong together here: a Roman torque beside a Persian dagger, coins with Chinese characters next to an idol carved by hands from another continent.

This isn't only Solomon's mine. It's a funnel for plundered history, stored like trophies and tax.

Behind a curtain of stone beads you find another doorway, carved with a relief of a man holding a ring and a key. The ring opens. The key closes forever.

The lesson is clear: choose your ending before you touch the object that decides it.

You return your attention to the sealed chest. Curiosity wins, because it always does.

S25.text:
You take the signet ring and the vault seems to breathe out.

The mineral veins dim slightly, satisfied or disappointed, you can't tell. The ring is warm in your palm like a living thing curled against your skin.

When you slide it onto your finger, it fits perfectly, which should be impossible. Your skin tingles. The hair on your arms rises.

A quiet click answers from somewhere in the vault door mechanism. Time starts moving again. The mine doesn't like lingering once a choice is made.

If Sable is with you, their eyes lock on your hand. 'That's the key,' they whisper. Awe in their voice makes the ring feel hungry.

A thin vapor curls from the floor grooves, not lethal yet, just a warning: leave now.

You don't run. You move fast and steady, because running is what traps expect.

S26.text:
You slip through the hidden doorway, because you're an adventurer and that means you negotiate with your worst instincts daily.

The passage is smoother, built later. The air is hotter. The amber glow becomes steadier, like a lamp that never goes out.

It leads to a small chamber holding a clay tablet under a glass dome. The tablet is ringed with the seal repeated like a chant.

It isn't treasure. It's instruction. A manual for the ring, for the vault, for the system Solomon built to protect wealth by making the protection itself valuable.

As you lean in, the glass fogs with your breath and the script seems to shift, reflecting your expectations back at you. A psychological trap designed to keep you staring until the door seals.

Behind you, stone grinds softly. The doorway is closing.

Stay and learn, or leave and live. The mine tests curiosity as much as greed.

choices.label: BREAK THE GLASS AND TAKE THE TABLET

S27.text:
You move the tunnels without sprinting, the way you move when you know panic will kill you faster than any blade.

The mine shifts behind you, not collapsing—adjusting. Cooler air returns in increments as you climb.

You pass the bridge and the pool's eye-like reflection. You pass timbers and rails and the places where other people left blood as punctuation.

On the ladder, your hands shake. The ring warms against your skin as if it recognizes the ascent.

At the boundary where graffiti ends and clean stone begins, you realize how thin the line is between a tourist underworld and a vault built to punish ambition.

You seal the grate above and taste paper and safety again, then remember you still have to escape the library and the city that sits innocently over this machine.

The ring feels heavy, not in weight, but in attention. You are now carrying a reason for other people to kill.

S28.text:
You stop and turn back because you can't stand being hunted by a faceless threat.

Sable steps into your light like they were always going to, calm as a banker, dangerous as a blade.

'Hand it over,' they say, nodding at your hand. Their tone is almost gentle, which is what makes it terrifying.

They tell you a half-truth dressed as kindness: they can use it without being eaten alive by it, and you want to go back to normal life even if you pretend you don't.

The ring warms, reacting to threat, and with that warmth comes capability—command—shortcut power that tempts you toward a version of yourself you might hate.

You can fight, bargain, or use the ring on a hidden seal you suddenly notice on the rock, faint and waiting.

In this mine, every confrontation has a mechanism.

choices.label: USE THE RING ON A HIDDEN SEAL

S29.text:
You return to the secret chamber beneath the library with the ring hidden and your nerves stretched thin as wire.

Upstairs, the library feels quiet but not empty. You sense someone near the front desk pretending to browse, waiting for you to make a mistake.

You tuck the book under your arm and keep your pace steady. Running makes you memorable. And in a city like this, being memorable to the wrong people is a death sentence with paperwork.

At the exit, the clerk's eyes flick to your hand. The pause is half a second too long. They say, 'Enjoy your reading,' and the words land like a message for someone listening.

Outside, Paris is bright and indifferent. Cafes chatter. Scooters buzz. The city doesn't care what is under it, and that ignorance feels like a gift.

You walk three blocks before you let yourself breathe. You have something that belongs to a story older than this city, and now you decide whether you keep it, hide it, or use it.

The ring warms on your finger like a heartbeat asking for permission.

choices.label: USE IT TO OPEN THE NEXT DOOR

S30.text:
You press the signet ring to a faint seal hidden on the wall, and heat surges through the metal like a breath taken too deep.

The rock vibrates. A seam appears where there was none. The mine isn't just a vault. It's a network.

Sable stares, their practiced calm cracking. 'You didn't tell me it could do that,' they say, and you hear addiction in the word 'could.'

The wall opens onto a narrow passage lit by steady amber light that doesn't come from torches. The air beyond smells cleaner, colder, like paper kept in a room no one has breathed in for years.

You step to the threshold and feel the world tilt in concept. The ring isn't only a key to treasure. It's a key to hidden places built by people who believed in systems of secrecy and power.

Behind you, the mine settles, satisfied you learned the lesson. Ahead, a new corridor waits, and you sense a lifetime of doors you could open if you choose to become that person.

This is the moment legends are born: not when you take gold, but when you decide you will keep walking even after you should have stopped.

END_GOOD.text:
GOOD ENDING — YOU ESCAPE WITH THE REAL TREASURE: YOUR LIFE

You leave Paris with the signet ring hidden where no one would think to look, and you do something rare for your profession: you stop.

You disappear into ordinary routines on purpose. You change flights. You change names. You let the book become just another object on a shelf, and the ring become a secret you carry like a scar.

Some nights you wake thinking you hear the mine breathing. Other nights you dream of doors opening at the touch of your hand. The hardest lesson is living with a key you refuse to use.

But you also learn something calmer: you can choose not to be owned by what you found. You can let a legend stay buried.

Somewhere beneath Paris, the vault waits for the next thief. This time, it doesn't get you.

END_BAD.text:
BAD ENDING — THE MINE COLLECTS ITS DUE

Something goes wrong in the way things always go wrong when greed meets mechanism.

A trap breathes poison. A doorway seals while you're still inside it. A rival's blade finds you in a corridor that doesn't echo screams back to the surface.

Paris keeps moving above you, unaware. Tourists sip coffee. Lovers argue on bridges. The city shrugs off your disappearance the way it shrugs off rain.

Down below, the mine folds your story into itself. Your footprints become another line in the roster, another symbol carved beside a name no one will pronounce correctly again.

Someone will find a book someday and feel the same spark you felt. The map will unfold. The descent will begin again. Legends stay alive because they feed.

END_SPECIAL.text:
SPECIAL ENDING — THE KEY TO THE NEXT VAULT

You keep the signet ring on your finger and feel it settle into you like a decision made permanent.

You don't sell it. You don't bury it. You learn it. You test it. You find the faint seals hidden in old places and realize the world is stitched together with doors most people never see.

The mine under Paris was not the destination. It was the first chapter in a system built to outlive empires: locked rooms, sealed archives, and vaults that protect knowledge people were willing to kill to keep secret.

One night, you return to the hidden chamber and press the ring to a mark you never noticed before. The wall opens without complaint, as if it has been waiting years for you specifically.

The air beyond is cold and clean. The amber light is steady. Somewhere far ahead, you hear a soft turning sound like a lock opening in a different world.

You step through and the passage closes behind you with gentle certainty. You are not just chasing treasure anymore. You are chasing the architecture of myth.
